UNIT_FINDING.detail: binary STL carries no unit declaration; the format has no field for one
basis: URDF lengths are metres by specification, and no scale attribute is declared on any of these meshes, so the mesh numbers enter the model as metres unchanged
the largest extent across all collision meshes is 0.2764, which is a plausible robot dimension in metres and implausible in millimetres or centimetres
UNIT_FINDING.NOT_ASSUMED: the unit is derived from the URDF contract and magnitude consistency, not from a convention about STL files

rule: a single convex hull is adequate for a link when its hull bounds equal the source bounds to within 1e-6 m on every axis, and its hull volume does not exceed the source volume by more than the preregistered inflation limit
a link failing the volume limit is a candidate for decomposition, not an automatic failure: the decision is recorded per link
SINGLE_HULL_ADEQUACY_RULE.limit_units: hull volume divided by closed-source volume
SINGLE_HULL_ADEQUACY_RULE.why_preregistered: a threshold chosen after seeing the numbers is a description of the numbers, not a test of them
SINGLE_HULL_ADEQUACY_RULE.clearance_caveat: volume ratio is a summary. A hull that bridges a concave gap can be within the limit and still close a gap the robot needs, so any link whose geometry is clearance-critical is reviewed on its own terms rather than on the ratio alone
SINGLE_HULL_ADEQUACY_RULE.articulation_rule: hulls are per collision element and never merged across links, so a whole-robot hull is excluded by construction

WATERTIGHTNESS.finding: several vendor collision meshes are not closed surfaces, and they include base_link and all four wheels. An enclosed volume is undefined for an open surface, so any volumetric adequacy test is unassessable for exactly the parts that decide the navigation footprint
WATERTIGHTNESS.consequence: this limits what any volume-based method can claim about those links, independently of which strategy is chosen

ADEQUACY_RULE_SELF_CRITIQUE.finding: the bounds half of the frozen adequacy rule cannot discriminate. A convex hull's extreme points are the source's extreme points, so hull bounds always equal source bounds and that comparison can never fail
ADEQUACY_RULE_SELF_CRITIQUE.consequence: the volume ratio is doing all the work. The bounds comparison is retained as a corruption check on the hull computation, not as an adequacy criterion

HULL_ADEQUACY.not_assessable_reason: volume ratio needs a closed source surface

OPTION_ANALYSIS.name: source triangle mesh used directly
OPTION_ANALYSIS.physx_note: PhysX triangle meshes do not collide with each other and are not valid for dynamic or articulated bodies. Every link here belongs to an articulation, so this fails on the actual engine rule rather than on preference

OPTION_ANALYSIS.name: single convex hull per collision mesh
OPTION_ANALYSIS.deterministic_basis: Qhull is deterministic for a fixed input and fixed options; the input is pinned by mesh hash
OPTION_ANALYSIS.conservatism: never smaller than the source, so containment holds by construction

OPTION_ANALYSIS.name: convex decomposition per collision mesh
OPTION_ANALYSIS.deterministic_basis: depends on the decomposer, its version, its parameters and its seed. Admissible only with all of those frozen and a reproduced digest
OPTION_ANALYSIS.conservatism: tighter than a hull where the part is concave
OPTION_ANALYSIS.cost: higher, and adds a dependency this repository does not have

OPTION_ANALYSIS.name: independently specified primitives
OPTION_ANALYSIS.source_basis: a vendor dimension table, CAD, or physical measurement
OPTION_ANALYSIS.why: no vendor dimension evidence exists in the acquired closure, CAD association is not established and conversion is not authorised, and nothing has been physically measured. Fitting a primitive to a mesh and calling it a specification would launder a mesh-derived value into a stated one

WHEEL_FINDINGS.FUNCTIONAL_NAVIGATION_COLLIDER: a hull of the wheel mesh gives the base a correct footprint for kinematic navigation
WHEEL_FINDINGS.boundary: a hull of a Mecanum wheel is a smooth solid. It cannot reproduce roller contact, and the source joints are fixed, so no version of this models Mecanum dynamics. Collision geometry loading is not contact fidelity

rules: each collider stays attached to the link that owns it
no two articulated links are merged
self-collision must not be created by construction

search_scope: all README and Markdown in the archive
VENDOR_DIMENSION_EVIDENCE.consequence: there is no stated dimension in the archive to build a primitive from. Any primitive this project produced would be measured from the meshes and then presented as a shape, which is a mesh-derived value wearing a specification's clothes
VENDOR_DIMENSION_EVIDENCE.note: figures such as an 80 mm wheel diameter appear in Yahboom's public product pages, which are not part of the acquired closure and are not cited as evidence here. Asking for a dimension table is already in the held support query

evidence_for: the file body contains the string ROSMASTER-M3Pro 2 time(s), which survives a rename and is therefore independent of the filename
it was distributed by Yahboom in the same drop as the M3 Pro code
the authoritative URDF was written by the SolidWorks URDF exporter, and Parasolid is a SolidWorks-native interchange format, so a common CAD origin is consistent
evidence_missing: no geometric correspondence has been computed; that needs a Parasolid kernel and conversion is not authorised in this tranche
no evidence that it is the same configuration as the URDF -- same arm variant, same camera, same options
CAD_ASSOCIATION.why_split: the internal name is real independent evidence that this is the M3 Pro product. It says nothing about which configuration, and a 189 MB full assembly and an 18-link simplified description need not correspond part for part
CAD_ASSOCIATION.not_used_because: the selected strategy needs no CAD dimension, so the question does not arise. Raising configuration association to SUPPORTED would need a read-only geometric comparison that is not authorised here

PHYSICAL_MEASUREMENT_GAPS.why_not: this decision is about which source and which transformation are defensible. Whether the source matches the robot is a different question, and answering it requires the robot

EXTENT_VALIDATION_CONTRACT.containment: a generated collider must never be smaller than its source where conservative containment is required

controls.F_TWIN_1_SQUARED_EXTENTS: every extent squared, as measured historically, is refused DIMENSION_MISMATCH
controls.POSITIVE_CONTROL: a correct collider set is admitted, so the check can pass as well as fail
controls.UNIT_SCALE: x1000, /1000, x100 and /100 are refused and named as unit errors rather than geometry errors
controls.AXIS_PERMUTATION: the same extents on different axes are refused as ORIENTATION_MISMATCH, not as a size error
controls.CONTAINMENT: a collider smaller than its source is refused
controls.WRONG_MESH_SIMILAR_SIZE: a near-identical mesh from another link is refused on source identity, not size
controls.DROPPED_COLLIDER: a missing link collider is refused
controls.DUPLICATE_WITH_DROP: equal total count with one link duplicated and one dropped is refused
controls.UNEXPECTED_COLLIDER: a collider for a link with no source collision geometry is refused
controls.SWAPPED_SET_EQUAL_AGGREGATES: two links exchanging colliders keeps every aggregate identical and is still refused

NEGATIVE_CONTROLS.counting_is_never_sufficient: F-TWIN-1 passed a check that counted colliders. Three controls here hold the count constant and still require refusal

DECOMPOSITION_BACKEND.finding: trimesh exposes convex_decomposition and every backend it delegates to is absent, so the call exists and the computation cannot be performed
DECOMPOSITION_BACKEND.consequence: determinism cannot be demonstrated for a computation that cannot be run, and an undemonstrated determinism claim is not a basis for admitting a strategy

DERIVATION_BLOCKERS: a single convex hull exceeds the preregistered inflation limit on every link where the limit can be assessed, so the primary strategy does not apply anywhere it can be tested
the fallback needs a convex decomposition and no backend exists in either available environment, so its determinism cannot be demonstrated
THRESHOLD_NOT_MOVED: the 1.25 inflation limit was preregistered before any mesh was measured and is not revised here. Raising it until hulls passed would turn the test into a description of the result
FALLBACK_STRATEGY: controlled convex decomposition, per link, only where a single hull exceeds the preregistered inflation limit or closes a clearance-critical gap, and only with decomposer, version, parameters and seed frozen and a reproduced digest

FUNCTIONAL_VS_CALIBRATED.why: a hull is faithful to the vendor's mesh. Whether the vendor's mesh is faithful to the robot is unmeasured, and a twin that reproduces a model exactly still reproduces whatever the model gets wrong

CLAIM_BOUNDARY: this decides a source and a transformation rule. No collider was generated, no asset was built, and nothing was compared against the physical robot
